summary: A scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, Elizabeth J. Harris earned her doctorate at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and studied at the University of Kelaniya (~1988–1993) under Ananda W. P. Guruge and Y. Karunadasa. She held a post at the University of Birmingham (~2017).

Elizabeth Mills is an Indologist who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. She taught Rory Brendan Lindsay and taught Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto (attested 2020).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, Elizabeth Morrison studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, Ellen Neskar, Janet Gyatso, and Susan Niditch. She taught Alexander Macmillan, served as an instructor at Amherst College (1998–1999), and held a post at Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Paul Groner, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Geshe Wangyal. She taught John Powers and served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).

Elke Rogersdotter is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006). Her doctoral studies were supervised by Thomas B. Larsson and Bozena Werbart, with co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.
Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She held posts at Leiden University, attested in 2003 and in 2018 on the Editorial Board.
Elliot M. Stern is an Indologist and philosopher. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a Ph.D. candidate until 1988 and earned his Ph.D. by 1998.

Elliot Sperling was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied at Queens College and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Lynn A. Struve. He held posts as professor at Harvard University and associate professor at Indiana University (~1986–2015).

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Fred Pfeil. She held posts at Mount Holyoke College and at Trinity College, where she was associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).
Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who has held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist who held positions at the Sanskrit Pathashala in Vadtal (attested 1937), Baroda College (attested 1939), and served as a Pandit at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology, Emi Matsushita studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts at Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education (1994–1996) and Ohio State University (1999–2001).

Emil Rödiger was a linguist who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1821–1825). He later held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1826–1853) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1874).

Emil Sieg was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at Kiel and Berlin. He held posts at Berlin (1896–1908), Kiel (~1909–1920), the University of Göttingen (~1920–1935), and Göttingen Academy of Sciences (1920).

Emilio Teza was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Anton Boller (~1854–1856). He held posts at the University of Bologna (~1860–1867), the University of Pisa (~1867–1886), and the University of Padua (~1888–1912).

Emily T. Yeh works in Tibetology. She studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003), and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2004).
Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht School of the Arts and completed her PhD at Utrecht University in 1970. She held a post at the University of Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Dhaka (~1957–1960) and the University of Oxford (~1969–1973), and held a post at the Bangladesh National Museum (~1973–1991).

Encho Tamura studied at Kyushu and Kyoto universities. He was a professor at Kyushu University (~1963–1980; emeritus ~1980–2013) and Kumamoto University (attested 1980), also serving as director of Kyushu Historical Museum and Fukuoka Prefectural Human Rights Center.

Endo Asai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1946–1949). He held posts at Nihon Fukushi University, Rissho University (~1960–1998), and served as president of Minobusan University (~1998–2004).
